title: Palindrome Partitioning
summary: Find all ways to partition a string into palindromic segments using backtracking to explore every valid cut position.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body:
Given a string `s`, split it into segments where each segment is a palindrome (reads the same forwards and backwards). Return all possible ways to partition the string into palindromic segments.

**Example:**
- Input: `"noon"`
- Output: `[["n","o","o","n"], ["n","oo","n"], ["noon"]]`
- `["n","o","o","n"]` - All single characters are palindromes
- `["n","oo","n"]` - "oo" is a palindrome in the middle
- `["noon"]` - The entire word is a palindrome

sections.heading: Key Insight
sections.body:
Think of partitioning as making cuts. At each position `start`, you choose where to end your next segment. You pick an end index and commit to the segment `s[start..end]`. The only rule? That segment must be a palindrome.

This is backtracking: make a choice (commit to a palindrome segment), explore what follows, then undo that choice and try a different cut.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.body:
The algorithm explores all possible ways to partition the string. At each position, we try every possible palindromic prefix and recursively solve for the remainder.

**Checking for Palindromes:**
A string is a palindrome if it reads the same forwards and backwards. We check this by comparing characters from both ends moving inward.

**Optimization:**
We can precompute a 2D table where `dp[i][j]` tells us whether `s[i..j]` is a palindrome using dynamic programming, changing each palindrome check from O(n) to O(1).

approach: Start at position `start = 0` with an empty path
For each `end` from `start` to `n-1`, check if `s[start..end]` is a palindrome
If palindrome, add segment to path and recurse from `end+1`
Base case: When `start == n`, we've partitioned everything - save the current path
Backtrack: pop last segment and try a longer cut position

quiz.q: What is the time complexity of the palindrome partitioning solution?
quiz.explain: We have O(2^n) possible partitions (each position can have a cut or not), and for each partition we do O(n) work to copy the path and check palindromes, giving O(n × 2^n) overall.

quiz.q: How can we optimize redundant palindrome checks?
options: Use memoization to cache partition results
Precompute a 2D DP table where dp[i][j] indicates if s[i..j] is a palindrome
quiz.explain: Precomputing a 2D DP table changes each palindrome check from O(n) to O(1). We use the recurrence: dp[i][j] = (s[i] == s[j]) && dp[i+1][j-1].

quiz.q: What is the base case in the backtracking recursion?
options: When we find a palindrome segment
When start == len(s), meaning we've partitioned the entire string
When we've tried all possible cuts
quiz.explain: When start == len(s), we've successfully partitioned the entire string, so we add a copy of the current path to our results.
